position_note: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) departure on schedule
Last contact with Kuala Lumpur ATC; over South China Sea heading northeast. Transponder switched off shortly after (~17:21 UTC)
source: Wikipedia: Search for MH370 (contact time corrected to 01:19 MYT)

position_note: Military radar tracked the aircraft turning back; last military fix ~02:15 MYT near Pulau Perak / west coast of Peninsular Malaysia
source: RMAF announcement 12 Mar 2014 via Wikipedia: Search for MH370

position_note: First ATOC satellite handshake after disappearance (SDU reboot; published 18:25 MYT); consistent with position over South China Sea near the coast
Last scheduled GES handshake before the final log-on; BFO 252 Hz - highest in the sequence (published '00:10'; time base as published)
source: Inmarsat SU log via Malaysian government release May 2014

position_note: Final handshake (AES log-on request + acknowledge at 00:19:37 UTC); range defines the famous search arc spanning lat 20S to 39S per JACC. Public reporting often quotes '08:19'
column8: Holland 2017 arXiv:1702.02432; JACC via MarineLink 20 Jun 2014

position_note: Aircraft considered to have exhausted fuel at or just before reaching the seventh arc and was descending; a glide of up to ~120 NM beyond the arc has been conceded plausible. Total flight time from departure ~15.6 h
source: JACC via MarineLink 20 Jun 2014; ATSB/IG concession
